source.title: Number of Sets of K Non-Overlapping Line Segments

teaching.hint: How do the endpoint inequalities differ inside one segment and between neighboring segments?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Shifting both endpoints of the ith segment by i-1 converts mixed strict and nonstrict endpoint inequalities into one strictly increasing sequence.
solution_outline.approach: Order segments from left to right. Transform their 2k endpoints by those shifts, giving 2k distinct positions chosen from 0 through n+k-2. Return C(n+k-1,2k) modulo the prime modulus.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: Inside each pair the difference remains positive; between pairs the shift makes a permitted shared endpoint into two distinct increasing positions.
solution_outline.correctness: Every legal set has a unique left-to-right endpoint chain. The shift maps it into a strictly increasing 2k-tuple. Conversely, subtracting the shifts leaves strict inequalities inside pairs and nonstrict inequalities between them, with endpoints in 0..n-1. These inverse maps form a bijection, so the subset count is exact. The factorial denominator is invertible because 2k is smaller than the prime modulus.
solution_outline.complexity: O(k+log MOD) time and O(1) auxiliary space using products and a modular inverse.
solution_outline.pitfall: Shared endpoints are allowed; treating all original endpoints as distinct gives the wrong binomial count.

common_wrong_turns: Shared endpoints are allowed; treating all original endpoints as distinct gives the wrong binomial count.
source_fidelity_notes: Restated segment nonoverlap as interior disjointness, kept shared endpoints and unused points, and made unordered set counting explicit.
